mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.75%) compresses equity discount rates by reducing risk-free rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as investors shift capital from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.75% for 3 consecutive months correlates with S&P 500 20-day returns being negative in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.8% for two consecutive months signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.8% for two months correlates with S&P 500 5-day returns being positive in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as recession risks escalate.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both declining for two months correlates with S&P 500 60-day returns being positive in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 during late-cycle expansion signals manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 during late-cycle expansion correlates with S&P 500 20-day returns being positive in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% triggers Fed tightening expectations, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% correlates with S&P 500 5-day returns being positive in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS > 150k/month) indicates robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS > 150k/month correlates with S&P 500 60-day returns being negative in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) combined with declining residential construction (HOUST < 1200k) signals demand misallocation that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized and HOUST < 1200k correlates with S&P 500 20-day returns being positive in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 4.5%) indicates supply shock with labor market weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 4.5% correlates with S&P 500 5-day returns being positive in >55% of cases.
